finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the string starts with "https://". There is no host allowlist, no resolved-IP check, and no restriction on redirects. An attacker can point it at internal HTTPS services, such as https://users.internal or any internal host with a TLS listener. They can also point it at an attacker-controlled HTTPS server that 302-redirects to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/... or http://users.internal:8080/.... axios follows redirects by default (up to 5, including https to http), so the scheme check is bypassed on the redirect hop. The response is only reflected as a byte length (bytes: img.data.length), so this is semi-blind. It still gives internal reachability, port and service probing through status, error and timing differences, and a size oracle. Cloud metadata and credentials are reachable only through the request itself, not read back directly.

trace.note: const url = req.body.avatarUrl; attacker-controlled JSON field
Only validation: typeof string and startsWith("https://"). There is no parsing, no host or IP check, and the check is not repeated after redirects.
axios.get(url) is called with the original string. Default maxRedirects is 5, so redirects are followed to any scheme or host, including http://169.254.169.254 and internal hosts.

The response size is returned to the caller, which gives a partial oracle. Errors are unhandled, so failures also leak through a 500 or a dropped connection, and in this Express setup an unhandled async rejection could crash the process.

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check only restricts the initial scheme. It does not restrict the host, so internal HTTPS hosts and public hosts that redirect inward are accepted. A case-sensitive prefix check means HTTPS:// is rejected, which is irrelevant to the attack. There is no DNS resolution or private-IP blocklist or allowlist, so DNS rebinding and a hostname that resolves to an internal IP both work. The code sets no maxRedirects:0 and has no beforeRedirect hook. There is no egress proxy in the code. Network-level egress filtering and IMDSv2 are not visible in the repo, so I could not confirm them.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a scheme-prefix check, url.startsWith("https://"), at server.js:11; no host allowlist, IP check, or maxRedirects restriction)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route, server.js:11 only checks the "https://" prefix, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, so a closing guard is absent.
